composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for Gusto, so you must supply your own client ID and secret in a custom auth config.

need_own_app.answer: Yes. Composio offers no managed Gusto app, so you register your own application with Gusto and give Composio its client ID and secret. Production keys only come after Gusto approval.

scenarios.label: Public integration for outside customers
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your AI agent connects Gusto accounts of customers outside your company using production keys.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count and required security documents, not measured

waiting.basis: No published review timeline was found.

scenarios.approval: Partnerships team reviews the Production Pre-Approval; if approved, the GRC team runs a Security Review. Approval is not guaranteed.

prerequisites.title: Security audit documents
prerequisites.detail: Gather current security audits (such as SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001 or PCI DSS evidence) and penetration test reports.

prerequisites.title: Track record with small businesses
prerequisites.detail: Gusto lists early-stage products without a track record serving small businesses as not currently supported.

prerequisites.title: Integration use case defined
prerequisites.detail: Gusto assigns scopes from your use case, so describe it precisely.

steps.title: Draft Production Pre-Approval application
steps.detail: Prepare use-case description and scope justification for the application.
steps.done_when: Draft is ready for you to review

steps.title: Submit application to Gusto
steps.detail: Submit with accurate company and business details.

steps.title: Wait for Partnerships team decision
steps.detail: Partnerships reviews first; GRC starts the Security Review only if approved.

steps.title: Test scopes in the demo environment
steps.detail: Test your assigned scopes in the demo environment and complete the Partner Checklist.
steps.done_when: Checklist completed and shared with Gusto

steps.title: Assemble security review documents
steps.detail: Collect audits and penetration test reports, then submit them.

steps.title: Wait for Security Review result
steps.detail: The GRC team reviews your submission.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your own client ID and secret, using the redirect URI copied from the Composio dashboard.

traps.title: Approval is not guaranteed
traps.detail: Gusto says production access is gated, not all applications are approved, and Pre-Approval is not a formality.

traps.title: Early-stage products may be refused
traps.detail: Products still establishing a track record serving small businesses are not currently supported.

traps.title: Scopes are fixed at review
traps.detail: Production calls outside assigned scopes are rejected. Scope changes after launch are requested by contacting Gusto.

traps.title: No test accounts in production
traps.detail: Gusto cannot support demo or test accounts in production.

blockers.what_it_means: Gusto issues production keys only after an approved Production Pre-Approval and quality review.
blockers.what_to_do: Complete Pre-Approval and the Security Review before launching to outside customers.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the application and checklist answers.

blockers.what_it_means: The call is outside the scopes assigned during review.
blockers.what_to_do: Contact Gusto to request additional scopes or scope changes.

evidence.answer: Composio lists Gusto under 'Bring your own OAuth app', so Composio does not supply a managed OAuth app for Gusto; the developer must bring their own.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: If the field does not contain that method, register your own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret.
evidence.answer: General rule: if a toolkit's composio_managed_auth_schemes field does not contain its OAuth method, the developer must register their own OAuth app and supply its client ID and client secret. This applies to Gusto, which is not in the managed list.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.
evidence.answer: This page is general and does not mention Gusto. It says Composio registers and maintains OAuth apps for popular toolkits such as GitHub, Gmail, and Slack.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You do not need to register your own OAuth app.
evidence.answer: For managed apps, the developer does not need to register their own OAuth app.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps are the default when they are available.
evidence.answer: Managed apps are the default when they are available.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: You provide your own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials and tell Composio to use them for a toolkit.
evidence.answer: Composio can provide a custom auth config where the developer supplies their own OAuth app, API key, bearer token, or other credentials for a toolkit.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Users will see "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.
evidence.answer: With a managed app, users see the consent screen text "Composio wants to access your account" during OAuth.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed apps share quota across all Composio users.
evidence.answer: Managed apps share their rate-limit quota across all Composio users; a developer's own app gets a dedicated quota.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval; your own app can use shorter polling intervals where supported.
evidence.answer: Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum polling interval for polling triggers.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Composio's default scopes may not include everything you need (e.g., write access to a specific Google API).
evidence.answer: Composio's default scopes for managed apps may not include everything a developer needs, for example write access to a specific Google API.

evidence.question: C1

evidence.answer: Self-hosted or regional variants of a service (such as a private Salesforce subdomain) need their own OAuth app rather than the managed one.
